questions.q: Design a multi-tenant SaaS application with Laravel.
questions.a:
Two approaches:

Single database (row-level):
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ All tenants share one database. Each table has tenant_id column.
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Global scope: TenantScope auto-filters where('tenant_id', currentTenant()) on all queries.
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Pros: simple infrastructure, easy migrations. Cons: data isolation risk, harder to scale.

Multi-database (database-per-tenant):
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Each tenant gets their own database. Central tenants table maps domains to databases.
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Middleware resolves tenant, sets config('database.connections.tenant.database') dynamically.
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Pros: strong isolation, can backup/restore per tenant. Cons: complex migrations, higher resource usage.

Key considerations:
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Domain routing: Route::domain('{tenant}.app.com') or header-based
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Cache isolation: prefix cache keys with tenant ID
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Queue isolation: separate queue per tenant or use tenant_id in job metadata
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ File storage: directories per tenant on S3 (tenants/{id}/)
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Testing: ensure tenant-scoped tests don't leak data between test suites

questions.q: Design a full-text search system for a high-traffic Laravel application.
questions.a:
Recommended stack: MeiliSearch (self-hosted or Cloud) + Laravel Scout.

Architecture:

1. Indexing: add Searchable trait to models. Override toSearchableArray() to include related data:
return array_merge($this->toArray(), ['category' => $this->category->name]);

2. Queue indexing: Scout auto-queues index updates via the queue connection. Configure scout.queue for async processing.

3. Search endpoint:
Product::search($query)
->where('category_id', $categoryId)
->where('price', '<', 100)
->orderBy('relevance')
->paginate(20);

4. Filterable attributes: configure in MeiliSearch settings for category_id, price, in_stock.

5. Typo tolerance: MeiliSearch handles typos by default Ã¢â‚¬â€ configure minWordSizeForTypos per use case.

6. Performance:
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Index only searchable fields Ã¢â‚¬â€ don't index raw HTML or logs
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Use separate index per locale for multilingual apps
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Re-index without downtime: build new index, swap atomically
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Monitor search analytics to tune ranking rules

questions.q: Design a multi-region, high-availability deployment for a Laravel application.
questions.a:
Architecture:

Infrastructure:
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ 3 regions (US, EU, APAC) behind a global load balancer (AWS Global Accelerator / Cloudflare)
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Each region: autoscaling group (min 3, max 20) behind ALB
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Database: Aurora Global Database (1 primary in US, read replicas in EU/APAC)
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Redis: ElastiCache Global Datastore for cross-region cache
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Session: Redis with read-replica failover
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Queue: SQS (global) Ã¢â‚¬â€ FIFO for order-sensitive jobs
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Files: S3 with Cross-Region Replication + CloudFront CDN

Laravel config:
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ SESSION_DRIVER=redis, CACHE_STORE=redis
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Queue: SQS driver
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Octane on RoadRunner for in-memory boot
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Read/write DB connections: 'read' => ['host' => $readHost], 'write' => ['host' => $writeHost]

Deployment:
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ CI/CD: GitHub Actions Ã¢â€ â€™ build Docker image Ã¢â€ â€™ push to ECR Ã¢â€ â€™ ECS rolling update
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Zero-downtime: blue/green deployment with health checks
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Migrations: run in CI before deploy, use --isolated for concurrent safety

questions.q: Design a caching strategy for a Laravel API serving 10M requests/day.
questions.a:
Layered caching strategy:

1. HTTP caching (Edge/CDN):
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ CloudFront/Varnish for GET endpoints
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Purge on model saved/deleted events via cache tags

2. Application cache (Redis):
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Cache::remember('product:'.$id, 300, fn() => ...)
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Cache tags for group invalidation: Cache::tags(['products', 'category:'.$catId])->flush()
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Cache-aside: app checks cache first, falls back to DB, writes to cache
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Write-through: on update, write both DB + cache

3. Query cache:
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ remember() on expensive queries: Product::where(...)->remember(60)->get()
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Use select() to minimize data transferred from Redis

4. Full-page cache:
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Static responses (docs, landing pages) served from CDN
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Dynamic pages use laravel-page-cache with Varnish/NGINX

5. Invalidation strategy:
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Event-driven: ProductSaved Ã¢â€ â€™ Cache::tags(['products'])->flush()
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Stale-while-revalidate: serve stale cache, refresh in background
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Versioned keys: increment cache version on deploy (atomic rollover)

questions.q: Design a multi-channel notification system with Laravel.
questions.a:
Approach:

1. Notification class: php artisan make:notification InvoicePaid
2. Channels: via($notifiable) returns ['mail', 'database', 'vonage', 'slack']
3. Each channel: define toMail(), toDatabase(), toVonage(), toSlack() methods
4. Queued by default: add ShouldQueue interface
5. User preferences: notification_preferences JSON column on User Ã¢â‚¬â€ checked in via()

Database notification: stored in notifications table. Read/unread tracked. Show in-app bell icon.

Edge cases:
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Rate limiting: implement withRateLimiting() to avoid API provider throttling
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Notification logging: NotificationLog model for audit trail
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Opt-out: per-channel unsubscribe links in email
Ã¢â‚¬Â¢ Batch sending: use jobs with tries=3, backoff for retry logic
